issues.description: Field SealSaloon.stock: the problem statement contains conflicting instructions about whether the stock field is instance-level or shared (static). In problem_statement.md (lines 69-71) the text says: "The SealSaloon needs ... a final Stock stock ... These should be initialized ... in the constructor of SealSaloon," which implies an instance (non-static) final field initialized in the constructor. Later in the same problem statement (lines 77-82) it explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static: "Note that the following methods and attributes must be static: - stock attribute ..." The provided reference solution implements the field as a static declaration: solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java (line 5) contains "private static final Stock stock = new Stock();". This contradiction (instance vs. static) can significantly confuse students about how to declare the field and whether related methods (acceptSupplyDelivery, calculateTotalPrice) must be static.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the specification inconsistency by choosing one design and updating all artifacts accordingly. If the intended design is a shared stock: update the earlier description (lines 69-71) to state "private static final Stock stock" (or "static final Stock stock") and note it may be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer; update the UML to indicate a static attribute and keep acceptSupplyDelivery and calculateTotalPrice as static. If the intended design is an instance-level stock: remove the requirement that stock (and the related methods) be static from the problem statement (lines 77-82), update the UML and example code to show an instance final Stock initialized in the constructor, and update the solution/tests to make stock non-static and the related methods instance methods. Ensure the problem statement, UML, and reference solution are consistent so students know whether to declare stock as static or instance-level.
